record.original_question: Determine whether the integer solution set of x^2 y + y^2 z + z^2 x = 1 is finite or infinite.

evidence.quote: The smallest open non-symmetric cyclic equation is x^2y + y^2z + z^2x = 1 (9) of size H = 25.
For this equation, we even do not know whether its integer solution set is finite or infinite.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Diophantine equation
$$x^2 y + y^2 z + z^2 x = 1$$
in integer unknowns $x, y, z \in \mathbb{Z}$. Determine whether the set of integer solutions $(x,y,z) \in \mathbb{Z}^3$ to this equation is finite or infinite.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was found for the equation x²y + y²z + z²x = 1 over the integers. It is identified as the smallest open non-symmetric cyclic Diophantine equation (height H = 25), and even the qualitative question of finiteness versus infiniteness of its integer solution set appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Search for results on x^2y + y^2z + z^2x = 1
status_evidence.snippet: No published proof or disproof of finiteness of integer solutions was located in standard number-theory references.
status_evidence.claim: The finiteness question for the integer solutions of x^2y + y^2z + z^2x = 1 appears open.
